raw.query: SELECT window_name, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(p99_ms) AS min_p99, MAX(p99_ms) AS max_p99, AVG(p99_ms) AS avg_p99 FROM provenance.v_pool_latency WHERE window_name LIKE 'burst%' GROUP BY window_name ORDER BY window_name
raw.observed: burst windows = burst1..burst6 (6, not 4); p99 ranges min 5.1 ms .. max 7,678,972 ms (burst1 avg ~119,166 ms). No row anywhere has window_name/run_id 'calm'/'day' (0 rows).
raw.claimed: "The four burst windows pinned at the 588 ms service floor; the calm day 548-734 ms."
raw.evidence: Burst windows are NOT pinned at 588 ms (588.37 appears in a few runs, but most burst runs are far higher, e.g. burst1 max 7.6e6 ms, burst2 56k, burst3 54k, burst4 116k); and there is no calm-day data at all.
raw.fix: Drop/rewrite the 'pinned at 588 ms floor' claim: burst p99 spans 5 ms–7.7e6 ms, not a floor; and either supply the actual calm-day source or remove the 548–734 ms claim (no such window exists in v_pool_latency).
